Emperor Xuanwu, temple name Shizong, taboo name Ke, was the second son of Emperor Xiaowen.
世宗 is the temple name Shizong, not an epithet “the Grand Successor”; the literal field renders it correctly.
In the first month of year twenty-one, on bingchen day, he was made crown prince.
In the first month of year twenty-one, on bingshen day, he was made crown prince.
丙申 is the bingshen day, not bingchen (丙辰); the literal field repeats the same day-name error.
On wuchen he raised his birth mother to Empress Wenzhao.
On wuchen he posthumously honored his late mother as Empress Wenzhao.
追尊 means to honor posthumously and 皇妣 is the deceased imperial mother; the idiomatic field drops the posthumous sense (the literal field has it).
Goryeo, Tuyuhun, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.
Goguryeo, Tuyuhun, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.
高麗 here is the Korean state Goguryeo (as rendered in s0011), not the later Goryeo; the literal field has the same anachronism.

On the first day of the third month, yiwei, he ordered every extraordinary levy beyond the regular tax remitted for the years of war.
乙未 is the yiwei day, not yimao (乙卯); the literal field repeats the same day-name error.

On jichou he drafted a hundred thousand men from the six provinces of Ding, Ji, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Si to reinforce the southern army.
